title: Join multiplied backups and incidents
description: Fix the query. For each server_name return the actual number of failed_backups and the actual number of open_incidents. Backups reach a server through databases; incidents use server_id directly. Multiple backups and incidents on one server must not multiply each other. Servers missing one event type must remain with 0. Return exactly three columns: server_name, failed_backups, open_incidents. Sort by server_name ASC.
starter_sql:
SELECT s.hostname AS server_name,
       SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_backups,
       SUM(CASE WHEN i.resolved = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_incidents
FROM servers AS s
LEFT JOIN databases AS d ON d.server_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN backups AS b ON b.database_id = d.id
LEFT JOIN incidents AS i ON i.server_id = s.id
GROUP BY s.id, s.hostname
ORDER BY s.hostname ASC;
hints: Aggregate backups and incidents separately before joining their results to servers.
Two CTEs or two aggregate subqueries remove the many-to-many multiplication.
solution_explanation: Pre-aggregation reduces each source to at most one row per server, making the final joins safe.
